items.title: Deny-by-default authorization from an explicit route→scope table
items.detail: Deny-by-default shipped as behaviour, and now as a table a test can iterate. `READ_SCOPES` and `WRITE_SCOPES` are exported and frozen, with `ROUTE_SCOPES` as their union. Making the check possible found seven mutating routes no prefix covered - `parametric-rules`, `trigger-protocols`, `report-distributions` and `report-schedule-runs` - each of which had been failing closed to `admin:*` and 403ing a caller holding the scope the documentation named. `scopeForRoute` matches on a `/` boundary, so `/api/v1/parametric` never covered `/api/v1/parametric-rules`: the safe direction, and the reason a prefix fails silently. `GET /api/v1/health` reports `configured`, `enforced` and the public-path list, which is the one route an operator can reach without a token to begin with.

items.title: Honesty envelopes on every numeric response, policed in CI
items.detail: Shipped as `honestyEnvelope` (`src/analytics.js:67`), applied to six numeric record types in that module — `flood_risk_score` (`src/analytics.js:896`), `climate_conflict_risk_score` (`src/analytics.js:1035`), `compound_hazard_risk` (`src/analytics.js:1101`), `service_impact_score` (`src/analytics.js:1176`), `calibration_summary` (`src/analytics.js:1259`) and `data_quality_confidence` (`src/analytics.js:1366`) — plus `trust_score` from `src/calibration.js:374`. Each carries value/limits/evidence/not_included, with `not` drawn from a declared `ENVELOPE_KINDS` registry. The audit's before-state: the caveat travelled with the number on exactly one route (GET /api/v1/flood-probability/score returned uncertainty.by_feature with contingency counts and Wilson intervals), no response carried the standard envelope, and `evidence{source_ids,basis_doc,retrieved_at}` and `not_included[]` appeared nowhere in `src/`. The CI rule the audit found absent is `scripts/check-no-flood-probability.mjs` (311 lines of blocked-vocabulary scanning, `:61`, `:142`); the envelope's own guard is `test/honesty-envelope.test.js` plus `check:model-boundaries`, which fails the build if a null is rendered where a refusal belongs.
items.note: honestyEnvelope() in src/analytics.js, applied to all five numeric record types the module produces, with `not` drawn from a declared ENVELOPE_KINDS registry so a number always travels with what it is not. Every prose `limits` string is kept beside it. Guarded by test/honesty-envelope.test.js and by check:model-boundaries, which fails the build if a null is rendered where a refusal belongs.

items.title: Per-region calibration and a trust score
items.detail: No alert_outcomes collection exists, nothing joins an alert to its outcome, and there is no trust score on any surface. What is present is the pre-existing tri-state honesty the entry cites as evidence, not the change: false_alert_rate is computed over determined or resolved alerts only and stays null otherwise (src/kpi.js:182-186, src/districts.js:166-168, src/equity.js:105-119), with the reason reported as a data gap (src/kpi.js:229). No Wilson interval is applied to the false-alert rate anywhere.
items.note: src/calibration.js, reusing wilsonInterval, MIN_MONTHS, MIN_EVENTS and MODEL_BASIS from flood-probability.js rather than reimplementing the model. Below thirty resolved alerts, or all-one-class, or non-finite, it returns null plus a reason: a score of 12 off four alerts reads as a measurement rather than as an absence of one. Served at GET /api/v1/calibration/by-region, which counts the refusals alongside the scores. test/calibration-trust.test.js.

items.title: Three tiers of uncertainty on every number
items.detail: One of the three tiers exists, on one route. Sampling is carried per feature as a Wilson interval with months_above_threshold beside it (src/flood-probability.js:298, src/flood-probability.js:332-340, surfaced at src/routes/risk.js:222-230) and is tested against the payload at test/flood-score-honesty.test.js:146-188. The model tier is absent — the Hessian is used only as a Newton step (src/flood-probability.js:400-412) and the fit returns coefficients with no standard errors or covariance (src/flood-probability.js:434-443), so nothing measures parameter uncertainty. The coverage tier is absent as a named list, and the effective-n correction for the serial correlation of overlapping windows is not implemented: wilsonInterval is called with the raw above.length (src/flood-probability.js:296-298).
items.note: uncertaintyTiers returns model_parameter, sampling and coverage, each named for what it measures. effectiveSampleSize does the AR(1) correction for the overlapping 90-day windows. A test asserts no tier's JSON contains 'confidence interval' or 'predictive interval'. Both model and sampling tiers return a refusal string, because none of these scores is a fitted model over contingency counts, and the sensitivity band stays outside all three tiers per ADR-004.

items.title: Model-drift monitoring
items.detail: No evidence outside the spec itself. There is no drift flag on any score, no model_drift_events collection, and no /api/v1/model-drift route; a repo-wide search for model.drift, drift_flag and drift_events matches only docs/improvements/enhancements.md:134-135 and the research note. The cited data-age concept does exist and is untouched by any model monitoring — freshnessPenaltyFor (src/analytics.js:470) is called once, for source staleness in a confidence score (src/analytics.js:354), and nothing compares a stored coefficient vector against a training run.
items.note: src/drift.js: PSI per feature plus predicted-versus-observed divergence, four verdicts. Computed on every refresh and stored in the derived set, served at GET /api/v1/model-drift. Never reported from a single observation, and divergence only when the observed rate's Wilson interval excludes the predicted mean. All seven regions currently refuse with the reason attached — 'input shift needs >= 24 months in each window'. test/drift-monitoring.test.js.
